initial_build_notes.text:
Implementation contract (short):

- Requirement indices -> owning files:
  - 0 (title): game/crumb_chase.py
  - 1 (15x15 grid maze): game/maze.py (generation) + game/crumb_chase.py (render)
  - 2 (green mouse): game/entities.py (Mouse) + game/crumb_chase.py (render)
  - 3-4 (arrow keys & continuous tile movement): game/crumb_chase.py + game/entities.py (Mouse movement)
  - 5-7 (crumbs, score): game/crumb_chase.py (crumb set and scoring) + game/entities.py (Crumb)
  - 8-10 (cats move, one tile at a time, junction logic milestone 2 partially implemented in Cat): game/entities.py (Cat logic) + game/crumb_chase.py (timing)
  - 11-16 (collisions, lives, win/lose, HUD, restart, quit): game/crumb_chase.py
  - 17-21 (console prints and plain shapes): game/crumb_chase.py (prints + shape drawing)

- State ownership and interfaces:
  - Maze (game/maze.py: Maze): owns grid boolean matrix. Methods:
    - Maze(width:int=15,height:int=15)
    - reset(): -> None (regenerates grid)
    - is_open(x:int,y:int) -> bool
    - neighbors(x:int,y:int) -> List[(x,y)]
    - all_open_tiles() -> List[(x,y)]
  - Entities (game/entities.py):
    - class Mouse:
      - mouse.tile: (int x,int y)
      - mouse.dir: (dx,dy) or None
      - mouse.px,py: float pixel position
      - Mouse(start_tile:(x,y), tile_size:int, speed_tiles_per_sec:float)
      - update(dt:float, maze:Maze) -> None (moves toward current dir until wall)
      - set_dir(dx,dy) -> None
      - teleport(tile) -> None
    - class Cat:
      - Cat(start_tile, tile_size, speed_tiles_per_sec)
      - update(dt, maze, mouse_tile) -> None (one tile at a time; at junction chooses neighbor reducing Manhattan distance)
      - teleport(tile)
    - class Crumb:
      - Crumb(tile:(x,y)); attribute eaten:bool
  - game/crumb_chase.py orchestrates input->action->state->render and owns score, lives, game_state. Public functions:
    - run() -> None (entry point)
    - reset_game() -> None (rebuilds maze, crumbs, resets entities)

- Coordinates:
  - Tile coordinates: (tx,ty) integers with (0..14,0..14); origin top-left. Pixel positions computed to tile center: px = hud + ty*tile_size + tile_size/2 (note y/h logic in code).
  - Movement uses pixel positions; a tile is reached when entity pixel pos is within small epsilon of target center; collisions are checked on tile coordinates.

- Lifecycle:
  - init: Maze, entities, crumbs created; score=0, lives=3, state='PLAY'
  - play: arrow keys set mouse direction (prints TURN ...). Mouse moves continuously tile-by-tile until wall; cats move one tile at a time every tile interval and choose towards mouse at junctions.
  - collision: if cat tile == mouse tile -> lives--, teleport everyone to starts; if lives==0 -> state='GAME_OVER' freeze, print "GAME OVER"
  - win: if crumbs empty -> state='WIN' freeze, print "WIN"
  - reset (R): rebuilds maze and crumbs, reset score/lives/positions, print "RESTART"
  - quit (Escape or window close): print "QUIT" and exit.

Now I will write the promised files implementing the above.

requirement_coverage.check: The game window title displays 'Crumb Chase'.
The game displays a grid of 15x15 tiles with walls.
A green shape representing the mouse is visible on the screen.
Pressing an arrow key changes the mouse's direction of movement.
After pressing an arrow key, the mouse moves continuously in that direction until it reaches a wall tile.
All non-wall tiles initially display a small crumb shape.
When the mouse moves onto a tile with a crumb, the crumb disappears, and the score increases by 10.
Two distinct shapes representing cats are visible and move within the maze.
Cats move from one tile to an adjacent tile at regular intervals.
When a cat reaches a junction (more than two open paths), it chooses a path that reduces its Manhattan distance to the mouse.
When a cat occupies the same tile as the mouse, the 'Lives' counter decreases by 1.
After a collision, the mouse and both cats instantly teleport to their initial positions.
The 'Lives' display starts at 3.
When the last crumb is eaten, the game state changes to 'WIN'.
When 'Lives' reaches 0, the game state changes to 'GAME OVER'.
Text displaying 'Score: X' and 'Lives: Y' is visible at the top of the game window and updates correctly.
Upon winning or losing, 'WIN' or 'GAME OVER' text appears with the final score, and all game movement stops.
Pressing 'R' resets the game to its initial state: mouse and cats at start, 3 lives, 0 score, all crumbs present.
Pressing 'Escape' closes the game window.
The console outputs the specified text when the corresponding control is activated.
The console outputs 'WIN' or 'GAME OVER' when the game reaches an end state.
All visual elements are rendered using basic geometric shapes and solid colors; no image files are loaded, and no sounds are played.
